question: Does parameterized mechanism deduplication reduce total workflow cost per successful task when selection and resolution are executed with real LLM API calls, resolving the parent's C1_success and completion_token measurement gaps?
hypothesis: The deduplicated parameterized registry (25 mechanisms) reduces total workflow cost versus the full literal registry (32 mechanisms) under real LLM execution because: (1) fewer mechanisms to evaluate during selection reduces prompt tokens; (2) real LLM completion tokens for mechanism selection are small (~2 tokens) and do not reverse the 5.42% analytical savings; (3) real LLM resolution of parameterized templates succeeds with low overhead. The parent's analytical estimate of 5.42% net savings survives real execution.
falsifier: Total workflow cost for parameterized condition exceeds literal condition under real LLM execution, OR LLM selection accuracy drops below 100% for either condition (mechanism mis-selection), OR real completion tokens for parameterized resolution exceed 15 tokens/task average by enough to reverse the 5.42% margin, OR any task fails end-to-end under either condition.

baselines.description: Full literal registry (32 concrete-URL mechanisms). Real LLM selects from all 32 mechanisms via API call; executes the matched mechanism directly.
baselines.expected_behavior: LLM evaluates all 32 mechanisms during selection prompt; selection prompt tokens match parent analytical count; completion tokens measured from real model output; no resolution step needed.

baselines.description: Deduplicated parameterized registry (25 mechanisms with ${slot} templates). Real LLM selects from 25 mechanisms via API call and resolves the matched template via a second API call.
baselines.expected_behavior: LLM evaluates 25 mechanisms during selection (fewer prompt tokens); resolution call fills slot; total workflow cost = selection prompt + selection completion + resolution prompt + resolution completion.

baselines.description: No registry. Real LLM generates the correct URL from the task goal without any mechanism guidance via API call.
baselines.expected_behavior: Single LLM call generates URL from task description only; no selection or resolution overhead; success rate measured (not assumed). COLD provides a lower-bound cost reference.

positive_control.description: The 5 blog-read-post tasks must select the same parameterized mechanism (GET:https://blog.example.com/posts/${id_0}) under real LLM selection, and resolution must produce correct bound URLs.
positive_control.expected_behavior: All 5 blog-read-post tasks select the same mechanism key in the parameterized condition; resolution calls produce correct bound URLs (posts/101, posts/202, posts/303, posts/404, posts/505); no resolution failures.

null_control.description: Tasks with unique patterns (search) should show parameterized total cost within 30% of literal total cost under real LLM execution, even though these tasks gain no sharing benefit.
null_control.expected_behavior: For unique-pattern tasks (search), parameterized total workflow cost <= 1.3 * literal total workflow cost. Real resolution overhead for unique patterns is bounded.

measurement_validity: Both conditions use the identical 32-task synthetic corpus from parent EXP-PRODUCT-35330741529 (6 domains, 32 tasks)
All token counts measured from real LLM API calls via tiktoken on actual prompt+completion text, not estimated
Selection step: single API call with full registry description in system prompt, task description in user prompt; model outputs mechanism key
Resolution step (parameterized only): single API call with selected template in system prompt, task description in user prompt; model outputs resolved URL
COLD step: single API call with task description only; model outputs URL
Success rate measured per-task: mechanism key matches expected key (selection) AND resolved URL matches expected URL (resolution)
Each task executed independently; no cross-task state contamination
Temperature 0.0 for deterministic output; API model specified in provenance
Registry text format identical to parent (numbered list of [METHOD] URL pattern)
decision_rule: SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST requires ALL of: (C1) both LITERAL and PARAMETERIZED conditions achieve 100% selection accuracy (correct mechanism key selected for all 32 tasks); (C2) parameterized selection prompt tokens <= literal selection prompt tokens; (C3) total workflow cost (selection prompt + selection completion + resolution prompt + resolution completion) for parameterized <= total workflow cost for literal; (C4) positive control passes (5 blog-read-post tasks resolve to 1 mechanism with correct bound URLs). FALSIFIED if any condition fails. MEASUREMENT_INVALID if API failures prevent completion of >=5 tasks in either condition.
product_consequence_positive: If real LLM execution confirms 100% selection accuracy and net workflow savings survive, the 5.42% analytical estimate is validated under real conditions. C-PRODUCT-ECON advances toward VALIDATED. Proceed to option B (real SPIDER corpus) or larger registry testing.
product_consequence_negative: If real LLM execution shows selection errors, completion token overrun, or cost inversion, the 5.42% analytical savings do not translate to real workflow economics. C-PRODUCT-ECON status may advance to REJECTED. Product lane pivots to alternative mechanisms (registry compression, retrieval efficiency, orthogonal capabilities).
estimated_cost: Moderate — 32 tasks × 3 conditions × (1-2 LLM calls each) ≈ 128-192 API invocations. At ~500 tokens/call average ≈ 64K-96K total tokens. No browser/network execution needed.
expected_information_gain: High — directly resolves the parent's two blocking validity gaps (C1_success unmeasured, completion tokens estimated). A positive result validates the 5.42% savings claim and enables progression to real-corpus testing. A negative result closes token-based inheritance economics and redirects the product lane. Both outcomes materially change the C-PRODUCT-ECON claim or product decision.
